summary: Dynamic instrumentation changes or observes a program while it runs — injecting code, hooking function prologues, intercepting library/syscall boundaries, or attaching a debugger/tracer to read and write live state. For an agentic control plane it is the deepest technique family: it can call an app's internal functions directly, read live object graphs, and hook events the UI never surfaces, giving a de-facto API where none exists. The tools are individually mature (Frida 17.25.1 released 2026-11-01, Detours 4.0.1, JVMTI, eBPF uprobes in mainline), but a safe, generic cross-platform agent wrapper around them is not — that is the hard part this project would invent. Power is matched by platform hardening (macOS Hardened Runtime/SIP, Windows PPL, Linux Yama ptrace_scope, code signing, anti-cheat kernel drivers) built specifically to block injection and cross-process reads on software the user did not build, which must be treated as hard stops. REA ships a deliberately narrow, observation-biased Frida integration (8 MCP tools, never kills the target, caller-authored scripts recorded by hash only, bounded truncation-reporting capture, credentials excluded) that is a strong reference model for exposing instrumentation to an agent safely.
platforms: Linux (Yama ptrace_scope 0-3, LD_PRELOAD at launch, eBPF uprobes with CAP_BPF/root)
macOS (task_for_pid gated by com.apple.security.cs.debugger + target get-task-allow; SIP and Hardened Runtime block injection; DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES restricted; admin auth dialog, ~10h window)
Windows (SeDebugPrivilege for cross-process; Protected Process Light rejects user-mode debugger attach even with SeDebugPrivilege; code signing / anti-tamper)
JVM (JVMTI / java.lang.instrument premain+agentmain, ByteBuddy attach - cross-OS)
.NET/Mono (CLR profiler API ICorProfilerCallback, Harmony runtime patching - cross-OS)
Node.js / V8 (node:inspector + Chrome DevTools Protocol, --inspect - cross-OS)
Mobile/console/anti-cheat (frida-server needs root/jailbreak or owned debuggable build; ring-0 anti-cheat = out of scope / hard stop)
representative_tools: Frida — https://frida.re / https://github.com/frida/frida — wxWindows Library Licence v3.1 (OSI; confirm upstream LICENSE) — cross-platform scriptable instrumentation: attach/spawn, Interceptor, Java/ObjC bridges, Stalker, frida-server; latest 17.25.1 (2026-11-01)
LD_PRELOAD (glibc ld.so) — https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ld.so.8.html — LGPL/platform — Linux launch-time library injection, ignored for secure-execution binaries
DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES (dyld) — https://developer.apple.com — Apple platform — macOS launch-time injection, blocked by Hardened Runtime without entitlement
Microsoft Detours — https://github.com/microsoft/Detours — MIT (v4.0.1) — Win32 function hooking by trampoline
MinHook — https://github.com/TsudaKageyu/minhook — BSD-2-Clause — minimal x86/x64 inline hooking for Windows
EasyHook — https://easyhook.github.io — LGPL (selling modified source restricted) — Windows user+kernel hooking with .NET bindings
java.lang.instrument / JVMTI — https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/jvmti/ — JDK (GPLv2+CPE) — JVM-native agent interface, class retransformation
Byte Buddy (+byte-buddy-agent) — https://bytebuddy.net — Apache-2.0 — JVM bytecode gen + runtime agent attach to local/remote JVMs
.NET CLR Profiler API (ICorProfilerCallback) — https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/unmanaged-api/profiling/ — platform — native IL-rewriting profiler, env-var activated
Harmony / HarmonyX — https://github.com/pardeike/Harmony — MIT — runtime prefix/postfix/transpiler patching of .NET/Mono methods
Python sys.settrace / monkeypatching — https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.settrace — PSF — in-process trace hook and attribute rebinding
Node --inspect / node:inspector — https://nodejs.org/api/inspector.html — MIT-ish (Node) — V8 Inspector / CDP control, programmatic or remote
eBPF uprobes/USDT (bcc, bpftrace) — https://github.com/iovisor/bcc / https://bpftrace.org — Apache-2.0 / GPL-2.0 — kernel-mediated userspace tracing, observation-first, needs CAP_BPF/root
DTrace — http://dtrace.org — CDDL — dynamic tracing (illumos/Solaris/BSD; SIP-limited on macOS)
GDB Python API — https://sourceware.org/gdb/ — GPLv3 — scriptable native debugger (gdb.* bindings)
LLDB Python API — https://lldb.llvm.org/use/python-reference.html — Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions — LLVM debugger with full Python module
WinDbg / DbgEng (IDebug* COM) — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/drivers/debugger/ — Microsoft — scriptable Windows debugger engine
Rizin / r2pipe (radare2) — https://rizin.re / https://github.com/radareorg/radare2 — LGPL-3.0 — RE framework with r2pipe/r2papi scripting + debugger
strengths: Depth no UI/accessibility route can reach: call internal functions directly, read live memory, hook events the app never renders
Observation can be non-invasive: eBPF uprobes, DTrace, read-only debugger snapshots, Node --inspect on a process you launched
Works across language runtimes: native (Frida/Detours/debuggers), JVM (JVMTI/ByteBuddy), .NET (profiler/Harmony), Node (inspector), Python (settrace)
Scriptable and composable: Frida message passing, LLDB/GDB Python bindings, r2pipe map cleanly onto an MCP tool boundary
Spawn-paused + load-before-run (Frida spawn, Node --inspect-brk) gives deterministic instrumentation installed before any target code runs
Turns private internals into a de-facto API for software you own — shortest path from no-API to scriptable
failure_modes: Process instability/crashes: bad hook, wrong calling convention, mismatched struct layout, or stray write corrupts the shared address space
Undefined behavior from re-entrancy/threading: hooks fire on arbitrary threads, can deadlock or corrupt state
Version fragility: hooks keyed to offsets/symbols/structs/private APIs break on every target update — dominant maintenance cost and why adding a target is hard
Observer effect & overhead: Stalker and heavy uprobe/trace workloads slow targets by orders of magnitude (Collabora bench: uprobe ~680 ns/hit vs USDT <1 ns)
Permission denial: ptrace_scope 1/2/3, missing SeDebugPrivilege, no get-task-allow, Hardened Runtime, PPL, SIP simply fail the attach/inject
Partial capture/truncation: high-rate hook streams overflow buffers; naive send-everything wrappers OOM or silently lose data (REA caps + reports truncation)
Cleanup/lifecycle hazards: detach must unload scripts, restore trampolines, resume paused spawns without killing the target; failed cleanup leaves target stuck
Supply-chain/trust: frida-server, agents, npx-installed tooling run with target (or root) privileges — compromise = full compromise
Hitting a protection is a hard stop, not a routing problem: PPL/Hardened/SIP/anti-cheat denial must stop-and-report, never escalate
tradeoffs_vs_others: vs accessibility/UI automation trees: instrumentation is deeper and faster (call the function vs click the button) but far more fragile and permission-gated; accessibility is stable, needs no injection, OS-blessed, but only exposes the UI surface

vs computer-use/vision agents: vision is most general and robust to internal change but slow, probabilistic, and blind to non-visual state; instrumentation is precise and fast but brittle and privileged — complementary

vs CLI/IPC wrapping & documented plugin/extension points: those are preferred when they exist (stable, supported, authorized, no injection); instrumentation is the fallback when no CLI/IPC/plugin API exists

vs static reverse engineering (REA's core): static is read-only, no runtime authorization beyond file possession, no instability risk, but cannot observe live state or drive the app; instrumentation is the dynamic complement

Net: instrumentation should be a tier-3 capability behind documented APIs/CLI/plugins (tier 1) and accessibility/computer-use (tier 2), enabled only for owned/authorized targets and biased toward observation
integration_notes: Process model: load native instrumentation bindings lazily, only when a tool is invoked (REA createFridaInstrumentationProvider imports frida on first use) — keeps base server light, avoids pulling native deps
Session as first-class server-owned object: start -> load script -> status/messages -> unload -> close, with server-minted UUIDs; the plane owns sessions, not the agent
Separate discovery (list devices/processes, remote connection closed after) from action (start session)
Caller/agent-authored scripts, server-executed, recorded by SHA-256 path+hash only — never persist source bytes (REA load_frida_script)

Bounded, truncation-reporting capture is mandatory: REA fixes 16 MiB/session, 128 KiB metadata, 4 KiB type, 32 KiB text, 250k JSON nodes, depth 64, no runtime override, and names a cap only when it dropped data
Never kill; detach != terminate: unload scripts and detach, resume a paused spawn only after cleanup confirmed, report final target state as unknown (REA close_frida_session)
Spawn-paused for determinism: leave target paused until explicit resume so scripts load before any target code runs
Credentials per-call only, excluded from evidence: remote endpoint token/certificate/origin used for that call/session, never returned or recorded
Pre-flight permission state (ptrace_scope value, PPL status, get-task-allow) and present one explicit authorization prompt per target; do not retry-escalate
Latency: spawn+load sub-second to seconds; Stalker/heavy tracing dominates; REA uses 1000 ms device-lookup timeout and bounded duration_ms (max 60 s) for one-shot
State: sessions in-memory, die with the server; failed cleanup retains handles for retry with visible cleanup errors

Per-runtime adapters behind one registry: prefer Node node:inspector/CDP, JVM JVMTI/ByteBuddy, .NET profiler, Python settrace over native Frida for managed targets — cleaner, more stable, often no special OS privilege for a process you launched
authorization_and_legal_notes: Scope: instrumentation is for software the user builds, owns the source of, or has explicit written authorization to instrument; NOT for defeating DRM/license checks, extracting protected assets, or evading security controls (matches REA DISCLAIMER.md)

Platform protections are hard stops: SIP, Hardened Runtime without your own entitlement, PPL, code signing/anti-tamper, and anti-cheat kernel drivers are deliberate vendor protections — stop and report, never route around (do not disable SIP, sign a PPL debugger, or load a kernel driver to reach a protected process)
Possession != permission: public availability, having a file, or access to a debug endpoint does not establish permission for every operation (REA DISCLAIMER.md verbatim stance)

Supply-chain trust: frida-server, native agents, npx-installed tooling run at target (or root) privilege — pin versions, verify hashes/signatures/lockfiles, avoid blind npx; REA pins Frida Core 17.23.2, ships a lockfile, native binding is optional+lazy

Licensing of bridged tools spans permissive (Detours MIT, MinHook BSD-2, Harmony MIT, LLDB Apache-LLVM) to copyleft (GDB GPLv3, EasyHook LGPL with source-sale restriction, Frida wxWindows-with-exception, DTrace CDDL) — bundling/distribution must honor each; commercial REs (IDA, Hopper, JEB) need independent licenses, REA grants none

Safety rails for an agent driving arbitrary software (from REA's design): observation-biased defaults, never terminate target, scripts recorded by hash with review before run, bounded truncation-reporting capture, explicit per-target authorization gate, credentials never persisted, refuse-and-report on protection boundaries, reclaimable sessions with visible cleanup failures
Jurisdiction: reverse engineering/instrumentation may be restricted by local law, software license, or ToS even for software you possess; user is responsible for authorization and compliance
open_questions: Generic add-a-new-target workflow: how the registry captures per-target knowledge (symbol maps, struct layouts, de-facto-API functions) in a form that survives app updates — version fragility has no clean general answer

Managed-runtime routing: concrete stability/privilege/latency tradeoffs of Node --inspect/CDP vs Frida, JVMTI/ByteBuddy vs Frida Java bridge, .NET profiler vs Harmony for agent use — needs hands-on measurement
LD_PRELOAD / DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES exact behavior under glibc secure-execution and macOS Hardened Runtime not re-verified byte-for-byte this pass
macOS DTrace under current SIP: what remains usable on a stock SIP-on Mac for software you built
Frida upstream license: confirm frida/frida-gum and frida/frida-core LICENSE files directly (identification here from forks + SPDX/OSI)

Pre-flight protection detection: can the plane reliably detect PPL / Hardened / missing get-task-allow / anti-cheat before attempting attach, to refuse cleanly? likely per-platform but detection surface needs design

Safe action channel: letting an agent CALL internal functions (not just observe) is the highest-value, highest-risk capability; what review/sandbox/dry-run model makes it safe is genuinely unsolved — REA sidesteps it by being observation-biased
